reasons: Only two of eight sections are visible, so most of the file cannot be checked.

terms.meaning: High-voltage direct current, a type of power cable link used for long distances.
Transmission carries power over long distances at high voltage. Distribution delivers it locally to homes and businesses.
A site where voltage is changed and power is switched between lines.
The main part of a name after generic words are removed, used to spot possible duplicates.
The category a project falls under, such as HVDC links or substations and converters.

sections.name: File setup, GridEuropeSegment
sections.title: Scope of the European grid cohort
sections.what: Explains that this is a second grid cohort covering the Nordic countries, Germany, the UK and the Netherlands, researched separately from the global grid cohort. It also defines the four segment labels.
sections.why: The header says the longlist was approved by the user on 2026-10-27.
sections.watch_out: The importer's duplicate check compares names, so a name change can create or hide a match without any visible error.

sections.name: GridEuropeIdentity, OSTWIND_IDS, otherOstwind
sections.title: Telling apart three similarly named projects
sections.what: Defines the identity fields, including the network type and a plain scope note. A helper builds each identity. Fixed IDs for three similarly named German projects let the importer exclude the other two when checking each one.
sections.why: The header says the Ostwind rows share a name core, so fixed IDs are needed to keep them separate.
sections.watch_out: The fixed IDs must match the ID recipe. If the recipe or a project key changes, the exclusion will stop matching the right rows.

sections.name: GRID_EUROPE_IDENTITIES (part 1)
sections.title: European grid projects, first group
sections.what: The first block of the European grid project list, covering groups eu-grid-01 through the first part of eu-grid-05. Each entry gives a project name, countries, site, a category such as HVDC Links or AC Transmission, and a scope sentence telling researchers what to include and what to leave out.
sections.why: Likely reason: the scope sentences stop researchers from collecting neighbouring projects, such as the later Ofoten to Balsfjord sections or a second London tunnel phase.
sections.watch_out: Some entries carry an optional extra label, such as distribution, that the code uses, but its exact meaning is not defined in this file.

sections.name: GRID_EUROPE_IDENTITIES (part 2)
sections.title: European grid projects, middle group
sections.what: The middle block of the list: the rest of group 05, then group 06 marked as under construction, then a set of group 07 to 10 projects added after a gap analysis. It covers German, Dutch, Danish, Nordic and British lines and links.
sections.why: The code comment says the expansion was approved for drafting on 2026-10-28, with the gap analysis kept in a separate document.
sections.watch_out: The gap analysis document named in the comment is not checked by this file, so the list can drift from it without any warning.

sections.name: GRID_EUROPE_IDENTITIES (part 3)
sections.title: European grid projects, later group
sections.what: The last content block of the list, covering groups 10 to 14. Group 13 covers German offshore and onshore HVDC lines still under construction, and group 14 is an optional pipeline of projects that are consented or in procurement but not yet under construction.
sections.why: The code comments say group 14 is for Opportunity Map coverage only.
sections.watch_out: The last entry passes a one-item list of an existing project ID, and the purpose of that list is not stated in the code, so check it before editing.

sections.name: GRID_EUROPE_IDENTITIES (part 4)
sections.title: Closing the European project list
sections.what: Ends the list, then builds a lookup from each project key to its entry. If any two entries share a key, the file stops with an error message.
sections.why: Likely reason: two entries with one key would silently lose one project, so the file refuses to load instead.
sections.watch_out: A duplicate key stops this whole file from loading, so one copy-paste error breaks the import for this group.

sections.name: GRID_EUROPE_COMPANY_NAMES
sections.title: European grid company spelling lookup
sections.what: Maps alternative spellings of five European grid operators, including Statnett, Fingrid, Energinet, Svenska kraftnät and Landsnet, to one standard name each, so each operator has one company row.
sections.why: The code comment says it avoids duplicate company rows.
sections.watch_out: Only the listed spellings are matched, and spellings that differ only in capital letters, such as Svk and SvK, must each be listed.

sections.name: GRID_EUROPE_POPULATION
sections.title: Settings for European grid import
sections.what: The settings that tell the shared importer how to treat the European grid list: its own population key, the industry name power-grid, location written as site and country, two extra cited fields for voltage and route length in kilometres, and two switches that change how company differences and follow-up findings are handled.
sections.why: The comments say the two switches exist for parallel research tasks and for follow-up deep-dives, and that changing any field changes committed plan digests.
sections.watch_out: Changing the population key renames the data folder and ledger for this list, and any setting change alters committed plan digests.

summary: Defines the list of European grid companies, lines and substations to research, with fixed keys, names, sites and segments, chosen so that they do not match the other grid cohort by name.
purpose: Identity list for the European power-grid population import, which runs alongside the global grid cohort.
why: The header says names and sites were chosen so the duplicate check cannot match the other grid cohort. It also says voltage and route length are asked for as sourced fields and never stored as fixed values.
how: Defines the identity shape with its segment, network type and scope. A helper builds each identity, with an option to mark names that are not duplicates. Fixed IDs for three similarly named German projects let the importer tell them apart. The rest of the file, which is not fully shown, lists the projects and their population settings.
inputs: None at run time. The list is typed in by hand.
outputs: A list of European grid identity records for the population import. The population settings file that these records feed is not visible here.
risks: Renaming a project can create or hide a duplicate match. The fixed IDs for the three German projects must match the ID recipe, or the exclusion stops working. Only parts of the file are visible here.
debug: If a grid project is flagged as a possible duplicate, check its name and the list of names it is marked as not duplicate of. If the Ostwind projects are merged, check their fixed IDs.
